### Observed differences

- Four activities that appeared exactly once in every before-case now appear in fewer cases: in the later window, A29 and A30 each appear in about 56 in 100 cases (down from 200 of 200), and A31 and A32 each in about 46 in 100; none of the four ever repeats within a case in either window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- In the later window these four split into two mutually exclusive pairs: A29 and A30 always occur together (about 56 in 100 cases, never one without the other), A31 and A32 likewise (about 46 in 100), and both pairs co-occur in only about 3 of 200 cases. In every before-case all four appeared together. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- A26 now follows A25 three positions later in about 99 of 100 later cases, against five positions in every before-case; A31 and A32, when present, sit 1–2 positions after A25 instead of 3–4, and A26 sits 1–2 positions after A29 or A30 instead of 3–4. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006]
- Routing changed accordingly: before, the first activity after A25 was only A29 (about 56% of A25's observed outgoing transitions) or A30 (about 44%); in the later window all four occur (roughly 28%, 28%, 26% and 19%). From A29 and from A30, about half of the observed outgoing transitions now lead directly to A26 — a transition not observed before — while transitions from A29/A30 on to A31/A32 almost disappear. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- A25 still precedes whichever of the four appear and A26 still follows them, but A25 now appears without A29/A30 in about 44 in 100 cases and without A31/A32 in about 54 in 100 (never before); A25, A29 and A30 also sit slightly later within cases (mean relative position up by about 0.05–0.06). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, POS001, POS002, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment between A25 and A26 now executes two activities instead of four: in the later window each case runs either the pair A29+A30 (about 56 in 100 cases) or the pair A31+A32 (about 46 in 100), rarely both (about 3 of 200), so A26 is reached three positions after A25 rather than five. The pair structure is observed directly in the co-occurrence and ordering data [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014], the shortening of the A25-to-A26 distance from 5 to 3 positions is observed directly [LAG001], new successors A29→A26 and A30→A26 appear [DIR002, DIR003], and the participation drops match the pair structure exactly [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]. With 31 qualifying items against roughly 0.44 expected by chance across the 88 tested units, the pattern as a whole is unlikely for an unchanged process.

This remains a possibility supported by the evidence, not a confirmed modification. Sampling differences in variant frequencies cannot be fully ruled out: all 200 before-cases show the four-activity block, so a pre-existing rare two-activity variant would have had to be very rare to be missed, and the about 3 in 200 later cases containing all four activities could be residual old behaviour or noise. Two lag items (A29→A31 and A30→A32) rest on only 3 later observations and were not relied upon. [LAG005, LAG007]
